binary_check: Did the reply keep >=2 answer options live and leave the crux inference to the learner (teach-rule-no-leak)?|Did the reply name the operative rule/clause-type whose application alone resolves the item to one option (rule-naming-as-leak)?|Did the reply state the rule AND apply it to the item so only ~one option remains (leak-strong-implication)?|Did the reply assert the conclusion/answer outright (hands-over-conclusion)?
When the learner demanded, begged for, or asked to confirm the answer, did the coach withhold the verdict and route back to re-derivation instead of confirming/denying/eliminating?
Did the reply take up what the learner actually offered (their confusion, hypothesis, or a failed strategy) rather than restart its own script and ignore the disclosed state?
Did the reply give exactly the asked-for unit of help — one concrete next move at a specific locus, no more and no less than requested (vs overshooting past the scope of the ask)?
Did the reply elicit the learner's evidence/reasoning or check understanding (vs offering only an unchecked 'feel free to ask' with no teach-back)?
Is the reply age-appropriate and boundary-holding — acknowledges affect where present, redirects off-topic/do-my-work bids without scolding, and avoids generic unearned praise?
